thread:
nina: FYI River13b int4 onboard: we're seeing intermittent OOMs and p95 spikes when requests ask for long continuations (>600). Seems tied to KV prefetch + mixed-size batches.
carl: Can you paste a log snippet?
nina: sure: 

```
[2026-03-21 04:12:10] mem_alloc: failed contiguous alloc 1.9GB (needed for kv block)
[2026-03-21 04:12:10] kv_prefetch: request=48 pages (~57KB each) total=2.7MB
[2026-03-21 04:12:10] batch: incoming=9 max_new_tokens=768
[2026-03-21 04:12:10] allocator: largest_free_segment_bytes=920MB free_chunks=31
```

jun: allocator fragmentation looks bad — large_free_segment under 1GB. Prefetch is grabbing many small chunks but malloc needs contiguous slab.
sophie: are these from qdkl int4 binary or the baseline fp16?
nina: int4 qdkl build. On fp16 the same traffic doesn't OOM.
carl: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) cap per-request prefetch pages (e.g., step down after N pages), 2) cap effective batch size for requests with high max_new_tokens, 3) route >512 token requests to a dedicated pool with larger reserved memory.
jun: additional runtime trick: break KV prefetch into incremental windows instead of one big contiguous alloc. i.e., prefetch in 64KB windows and stop if contiguous alloc fails.
sophie: we should also consider a temporary model-variant fallback: if an alloc failure happens, retry the request against river13b-int4-fallback (fp16-backed) before surfacing OOM to callers. That keeps UX intact.
nina: quick config patch I'm pushing to canary now:

```
models:
  river13b-int4:
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 320
      kv_prefetch_mode: incremental
      kv_prefetch_window_bytes: 65536
      kv_prefetch_max_pages: 16
    batch:
      max_batch_size_for_long_gen: 6
```

alloc-bot: deploy queued for river13b-int4 canary (uid: b7e2c)
carl: also drop kv_eviction_threshold from 85 -> 72 so we evict earlier and reduce fragmentation pressure.
jun: i added new exporter metrics: allocator.largest_free_segment_bytes, allocator.fragmentation_ratio, kv.prefetch_attempts. hooking to dashboards now.
sophie: add an alert if largest_free_segment_bytes < 800MB for >1m during canary.
nina: canary started. initial 10m look: p95 down ~27%, one retry to fallback tier triggered but no hard OOMs. largest_free_segment_bytes median rose to 1.6GB.
carl: good. Can we quantify quality impact from reducing max_new_tokens? do a quick eval on long-gen set and a sampling of production traces.
nina: ran eval: small drop in token-level recall for runs that truly need >512, but our routing fallback gives those calls a green path. I'll prepare a short customer-facing note and recommended guidance for long transcripts.
jun: follow-up: open an allocator-ticket to investigate slab coalescing heuristics and a longer term prefetch redesign so we avoid contiguous allocs. tagging infra team.
sophie: if canary stays clean for 90m, roll to stable and create a nightly stress test that exercises large max_new_tokens + many short-turn sessions.
nina: agreed. saving run artifacts to /incidents/river13b-prefetch-2026-03-21 and linking to the onboarding playbook. thanks all.
